_comment: Site profiles narrow the registry to what a given kind of site can actually
be judged on. An excluded item reports N/A with the profile as the reason and
leaves both metrics alone — it is out of scope, not undecided and not failed.
Exclusions are deliberately conservative. A check is only listed here when it
cannot apply, never when it merely tends to matter less: quietly dropping a
hard check would inflate the score exactly where the audit should push back.
exclude_scripts is resolved against the registry, so items stay in step with

default.label: No assumptions
default.note: The full registry. Use when the site type is unknown.

local.label: Local business
local.note: Physical premises or a service area. Local SEO applies in full; storefront-only checks do not.

exclude_item_reasons.CN-056: publication and updated dates are an editorial-content signal; a service page for a physical business has no publication date to show
exclude_item_reasons.CN-057: an author byline is an editorial-content signal; the publisher of a local business page is the business, which LocalBusiness structured data already states

local.script_args_note: A service page for a physical business says what it does, what it costs and where it is, and then stops. 300 words is the inherited default for a page with something to explain; measured against a real local site it called eight normal service pages thin (menu 189 words, blueberries 220, petting zoo 232) and buried the three that genuinely are (galleries, 74-94 words). 150 fails those three and passes the eight.

ecommerce.label: Online store
ecommerce.note: Product, category and faceted-navigation checks all apply. Nothing is excluded.

saas.label: SaaS or web product
saas.note: No physical location and no product catalogue.

exclude_item_reasons.AR-164: no product catalogue, so no product can go out of stock or be discontinued

blog.label: Blog or personal site
blog.note: Article-led. No storefront, no local pack.

exclude_item_reasons.AR-164: no product catalogue, so no product can go out of stock or be discontinued

media.label: Media or publisher
media.note: High-volume editorial. Storefront checks do not apply; ad-density and freshness checks matter more than usual and stay in.

exclude_item_reasons.AR-164: no product catalogue, so no product can go out of stock or be discontinued
